newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe board sacked over Malaysia power deal.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe board sacked over Malaysia power deal.

text.p: The Zimbabwean government has sacked the entire board of its power utility, ZESA, for opposing a deal with Malaysia to privatise the corporation, Transport and Energy Minister Simon Moyo said on Wednesday.

In a statement to state media, Moyo said President Robert Mugabe had approved a new 10-member board for the Zimbabwe Electricity Supply Authority (ZESA) in place of one which was pressing the government to rescind a letter of intent it signed last month with Malaysia power producer YTL Corp Bhd.
YLT would, according to the letter, invest Z$6 billion (U.S.$580 million) in the privatisation of ZESA's Hwange Power Station in northern Zimbabwe.

Solomon Tawengwa, the chairman of the sacked board, said the government had not informed ZESA of the deal which he said was a departure from an earlier government agreement to follow tender procedures.
Before the government's deal with Malaysia, ZESA had already invited bids and six foreign companies had been shortlisted, top of them a British firm, while YTL was at the bottom of the list.
Tawengwa was unavailable for comment on Wednesday.

But his board said last week it was also opposed to the agreement with the Malaysian corporation because it was contrary to the country's efforts to economically empower the majority blacks and would result in increases in electricity tariffs.

In his statement on Wednesday, Moyo -- whose ministry said last week the board was free to resign -- said because of this stance, Tawengwa's board would have found it uncomfortable to implement the Hwange project.
"The new board is expected to implement government policy with thorough dedication and professsionalism, in line with stated infrastructural development thrust in the energy sector," he said.
The new board is chaired by Professor Christopher Chetsanga, head of the Harare-based Scientific, Industrial Research Development Centre.
